earlier_scan.source_named: Only Comfort & Jakobi (2011) (verbal number, subclassification) cited on Glottolog elhu1238; no phonological description of El Hugeirat located

sources.citation: archive.org full-text search probes ('Hugeirat', 'Hagarat/Hagerat Nubian', 'Hill Nubian stress/tone', 'Kordofan Nubian stress', 'MacDiarmid Hugeirat'); CrossRef queries 'Hugeirat' and 'Kordofan Nubian'; ELAR site search 'Hugeirat'
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: All hits are name mentions in catalogues/surveys (Ethnologue editions, Voegelin 1977, UNESCO Atlas, Brenzinger ed., Moseley ed., Hofmann 1983, Sebeok CTL 7, Mann & Dalby Thesaurus); no snippet pairs El Hugeirat with tone/stress/accent; CrossRef has no El Hugeirat work; ELAR has no deposit.

sources.citation: Jakobi, Angelika. 2020. Nubian Verb Extensions and Some Nyima Correspondences. Dotawo 7; Jakobi & Hamdan 2015 (Karko, Dotawo 2); Ibrahim & Jakobi 2015 (Taglennaa, Dotawo 2); Comfort 2014 (Uncu, Dotawo 1); Hellwig & Schneider-Blum 2014 (Tabaq, Dotawo 1) -- sister-language papers already held by the project, a full-text search for stress/accent El Hugeirat
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: None of them contains El Hugeirat data or any statement about El Hugeirat prosody; they document tone (H/M/L, contours) in Karko, Tagle, Uncu, Tabaq only.

sources.citation: Alamin, Suzan. 2014. Noun Phrase Constructions in Nubian Languages: A Comparative Study. Dotawo: A Journal of Nubian Studies 1: 203-220 (whole-volume text already held by the project)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists 'Al-Hugeirat' among Kordofan Nubian dialects (fn. 8 -> Jakobi, Kordofan Nubian, unpublished ms); sec. 2.4 gives only a second-hand family-level remark that 'a tonal system has been found . Kordofan Nubian'; nothing specific to El Hugeirat and nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid elhu1238 (El Hugeirat) languoid record + reference table (6 refs: World Oral Literature Project; Moseley 2010 Atlas; Ethnologue 2009; Jakobi & Kuemmerle 1993 bibliography; Rouchdy 1991; MacDiarmid & MacDiarmid 1931), and Kordofan Nubian family kord1246 reference table (91 refs)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: zero descriptive references for El Hugeirat; the family-level list has phonology items only for Ghulfan (Czermak 1919), Tagle (Ibrahim & Huttenga 2007), Kadaru (Alaki & Norton 2013, 2015), Tabaq (Hellwig & Schneider-Blum 2014), Abu Jinuk (Alshareef 2015), Dilling (Sakran 1979) -- nothing on El Hugeirat.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'El Hugeirat language' (raw wikitext, stub citing Ethnologue 25)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; ~50 speakers (2007) in Sija, Bija, Shenishen, Baboy on the El Hugeirat hills.

sources.citation: Stevenson, Roland C. 1956-57. A survey of the phonetics and grammatical structure of the Nuba Mountain languages, with particular reference to Otoro, Katcha and Nyimang. Afrika und Uebersee 40: 73-84, 93-115; 41: 27-65, 117-152, 171-196.

sources.note: Contains the Hill Nubian group section with phonetic notes (tone/stress) that Tucker & Bryan 1966 drew on; would show whether any El Hugeirat material was included (probably only Kadaru/Dilling/Debri).

sources.citation: MacDiarmid, P. A. & D. N. MacDiarmid. 1931. The languages of the Nuba Mountains. Sudan Notes and Records 14: 149-162.

sources.note: The only reference Glottolog attaches to elhu1238 with wordlist content; Tucker & Bryan 1956 credit it for 'El Hagarat' material. Would confirm what primary data exist (probably a short comparative vocabulary, unlikely to state stress).

sources.citation: Jakobi, Angelika. n.d. (cited 2014-2020 as 'to appear'). Kordofan Nubian: A Synchronic and Diachronic Study. Unpublished manuscript, Institut fuer Afrikanistik, University of Cologne.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern comparative description covering the whole Kordofan Nubian cluster (contains grammatical sketches, e.g. of Karko, per Jakobi & Hamdan 2015 fn.1); if any first-hand El Hugeirat data with tone/stress marking exist, they are here. Coverage of El Hugeirat unverified.

sources.note: Group-level Hill Nubian remarks based on Stevenson's Kadaru/Dilling/Debri notes ('Little is known about tone.. In KADARU a few lexical tone doublets.. three level tones'); nothing on El Hugeirat, no stress rule.
